candidate_summaries.visual_intent: search/database contrast with one central access split
candidate_summaries.semantic_readability_basis: The frame is dominated by a single access-split composition: public portal on the left, private database depth on the right, and a locked threshold between them.
The frame uses a left-to-right pipeline: large private database stack, narrow extraction funnel, and a small public portal output.

candidate_summaries.visual_intent: property comparison board with overload pressure
candidate_summaries.semantic_readability_basis: A single comparison board owns the frame while excess candidate cards crowd its edges, so it reads as property comparison rather than sticky notes.

candidate_summaries.visual_intent: selected property with rejected cards and drawback callout
candidate_summaries.semantic_readability_basis: The layout has one selected property sheet in focus, rejected cards pushed aside, and a large drawback callout attached to the selected sheet.
A document comparison table leads into one green recommendation decision, making the scene feel like a recommendation derived from evidence.

candidate_summaries.visual_intent: AI recommendation system focused on one matched card
candidate_summaries.semantic_readability_basis: The AI panel is a dark system block with scan bars pointing to one highlighted property card, reducing whiteboard feel and avoiding product branding.

candidate_summaries.visual_intent: AI recommendation interrupted by risk warning zones
candidate_summaries.semantic_readability_basis: Risk zones are layered over the recommendation as warning bands, so it reads as AI/risk tension rather than a list of notes.

pass_fix_defer_table.reason: The frame is dominated by a single access-split composition: public portal on the left, private database depth on the right, and a locked threshold between them.
The frame uses a left-to-right pipeline: large private database stack, narrow extraction funnel, and a small public portal output.
A single comparison board owns the frame while excess candidate cards crowd its edges, so it reads as property comparison rather than sticky notes.
The layout has one selected property sheet in focus, rejected cards pushed aside, and a large drawback callout attached to the selected sheet.
A document comparison table leads into one green recommendation decision, making the scene feel like a recommendation derived from evidence.
The AI panel is a dark system block with scan bars pointing to one highlighted property card, reducing whiteboard feel and avoiding product branding.
Risk zones are layered over the recommendation as warning bands, so it reads as AI/risk tension rather than a list of notes.
